zh: 四万一千英尺。舷窗外是刺眼的白，阳光斜切进主舱，在胡桃木桌面上铺开一条滚烫的金。
奶油色小羊皮座椅晒出淡淡的皮革味，混着现磨咖啡的焦苦。引擎在脚底低低地嗡，震得杯里的冰块轻轻相碰。
两个人都默契地假装刚才那半秒不存在。Roman坐回对面，Adrian也坐下，胸口还在起伏，像刚爬完五层楼梯。
Roman靠回椅背。一身剪裁利落的黑西装，白衬衫领口敞着一颗扣，左耳塞着透明耳麦，螺旋线没进衣领。
他头发剃得极短，贴着头皮一层青黑，下颌一圈胡茬。那双灰眼睛冷得像结了冰的河面——此刻没在看Adrian。
敞开的领口下，一道旧疤从锁骨下沿斜斜探出来，颜色比皮肤浅。脚上的黑皮鞋擦得能照出舱顶的灯。
Adrian陷在对面座椅里，一米八二的骨架把扶手间撑得满满当当。借来的深蓝西装绷在宽肩上，肩线勒得他想骂人。
衬衫袖子被他胡乱卷到手肘，露出结实的小臂。脚上还是那双磨秃了头的旧工装靴，跟这架飞机格格不入。
很好。半分钟前差点亲上我发小，现在得坐这儿假装欣赏云。我是写文案的，不是演戏的。
他抬手搓了一把没刮的下巴，胡茬沙沙作响。喉结滚了一下，把那口没喘匀的气硬咽了回去。
桌上那台继承平板自己亮了，冷白的光打在两人之间。屏幕正中一行红字：需要二次身份认证。
第一题弹出来，字体干净得近乎冷酷：Adrian真正紧张的时候，会做什么？
Roman连眼皮都没抬，搭在膝头的手指轻轻叩了一下。
Adrian低头。他的右手不知什么时候已经扣在左手腕上，粗糙的拇指正压着那块凸起的腕骨，一下一下地揉。
连他自己都没察觉的小动作。隔了整整十年，Roman还记得，记得像昨天才看过。
该死。他连这个都记得——那他到底还记得多少？

zh.hint: 认证要求双方作答。平板转了个方向，冷光照上你的脸。轮到你答他的事了。

win.title: MATCH 92%
win.txt: 九成二。没有人会无意间，把另一个人记得这么细。

win: 平板炸开一圈粉色的光，映在Roman灰色的瞳孔里，一闪就灭。
剩下那8%，是我不在的那几年。
lose: 进度条停在一个不上不下的数字上，闪了两下。Roman扫了一眼，喉结动了动，没说话。
可他答的那几道，一道都没错。连Adrian紧张时揉的是哪块骨头，他都知道。

zh.hint: 认证结束，屏幕边缘又滑出一个粉色入口：情侣问答。三个私密问题，可以答，也可以跳过——怎么看都像陷阱。

opts.t: 你最想念什么？
then: Roman停了很久。他望着舷窗外那片白，下颌线绷出一道冷硬的棱，半天才开口。
你骂我的时候。没人敢那样跟我说话。

opts.t: 那天晚上，谁先移开视线的？
then: Roman的下颌猛地绷紧，咬肌在胡茬底下滚了一下。他没反驳。

opts.t: Adrian用拇指重重按下了跳过。
then: Roman盯着那个灰下去的跳过键，肩膀松了半寸，眼底却有什么东西跟着暗了下去。

zh: 界面又跳出一段烫金动画，流光从屏幕底部一路涌上来：欢迎礼遇·个人礼物额度。
你这么一说，我就一定要管了。
礼物页第一件是一块四万美元的表，铂金表壳在渲染图里亮得扎眼。昨天他绝不会点开，今天系统推荐得像推荐一杯咖啡。
可Roman不是会被价格打动的人。他只是想看Roman高兴——这个念头来得太顺，顺得非常不方便。
清醒点，Adrian。他是来上班的，你是他的工作。

zh.title: 猜他想要的礼物
zh.hint: 最贵的不一定最对。指尖悬在屏幕上——你还记得他多少？

then: Roman把衬衫袖口推上去，露出一截小麦色的手腕，一道发白的旧疤横过腕骨内侧。
Adrian替他扣表带。指腹擦过那道疤，皮肤滚烫，底下的脉搏一下下撞着他的指尖。
Adrian把扣环按到底，“咔哒”一声，这才抬眼。
只是想看看戴你身上好不好看。
Roman看了一眼褪色的布面封面，手指停在开裂的书脊上，指节微微发白。
他翻开扉页，十七岁的他用圆珠笔写的名字还在，笔画重得划破了纸。他合上书，很久没说话。
你连我紧张摸手腕都知道。扯平。
Roman把订阅卡收进西装内袋，靠心口那一侧，又用掌心压平了一下。
Roman把袖扣举到灯下，银面上的刻字反出一点冷光。他看了很久，目光却一次次落回桌上那枚Vale家徽袖扣。
同一个工匠。你从哪儿订的？
他的下颌收紧，太阳穴边一根青筋浮了出来。
Roman捏着那副耳机愣了一下，像从没想过自己还有不工作的时候。

zh: Roman从西装口袋里摸出一个旧钥匙扣，放进Adrian掌心。黄铜被磨得发亮，边角圆钝，还带着他的体温。
Adrian攥住它。金属硌着掌心的薄茧，那点体温顺着手掌一路烧上小臂。

zh.title: 回忆：他从没扔掉的钥匙扣
zh.txt: 明显在撒谎。黄铜磨成这样，得在掌心里攥上好几年。

zh: Adrian正想问他到底留了多久，裤袋里的手机猛地一震。金色通知铺满整个屏幕：未婚妻抵达——18:00。
通知下附着一张照片。蜂蜜色的金发梳得一丝不乱，炭灰色三件套，马甲扣子扣到最上面一颗。
他交叠在膝上的手戴着一枚家徽印戒，冲镜头笑得恰到好处——像橱窗里的奢侈品，连笑都标了价。
未婚妻。我连自己的银行账户都还没搞明白，就先多了个未婚妻。
他的视线从“未婚妻”三个字慢慢挪到Roman脸上。Roman表情纹丝不动，只有搭在桌沿的那只手停住了，指节绷得发白。

zh.hint: 一个凭空冒出来的未婚妻。比未婚妻更有意思的，是Roman那只停住的手。

opts.t: 帅吗？

then.hint: “帅吗？”他就是故意的。你知道他在看你怎么答。

opts.t: 不重要。
比我差。
then: Adrian愣了一秒，随即笑出声，那笑从胸腔里震出来，又低又哑。

opts.t: Roman把手机屏幕按灭。“我会查清楚他是谁。”
我结婚的话，安保也归你管？
then: Roman沉默了两秒。机舱里只剩引擎低沉的嗡鸣。
我负责让他活着走出你家门。

opts.t: Adrian什么都没问，只盯着Roman停住的那只手。
then: Roman把手收回去，五指慢慢攥成拳，手背上的青筋一根根绷了起来。
看看这只手。嘴上一个字不说，青筋倒是替他全招了。

zh: 前舱传来机长的声音，请他确认落地安保。Roman起身，西装下摆利落地一抖，走了两步，又回头。
你六岁的时候还更听话。
桌角，Roman那部黑色加密手机的屏幕亮了一下。照片缩略图一闪而过——是十七岁的Adrian，笑得没心没肺。
理智说不该看。另一半脑子说：他背着你看了你三年。“公平”突然成了一个非常顺手的词。
Adrian的手比脑子先动了。宽大的手掌压住那部手机，指腹上还残留着钥匙扣的温度。

zh.hint: 他在前舱，门缝里漏出他压低的声音。手机没锁屏。你大概只有一分钟。

items: 如果他回到Vale家，就说明你失败了。

apps.lockTxt: 需要密码。提示：便利店那晚的日期。
items: 十七岁的Adrian和Roman坐在便利店门口。照片里的Adrian还没学会带刺的笑，Roman也还没学会把情绪藏起来。
保存于十年前。此后每年同一天，被打开过一次。
我应该在今天之前就告诉他。
未发送 · 三年前 / 一年前 / 昨天
导航记录 · 布鲁克林某便利店 · 41次

win: 他把手机放回原位，角度分毫不差，连屏幕上那道舷窗反光都对准了。
他留着那张照片，整整十年。
比照片更危险的是那条草稿：他不是没想过回来，只是一次又一次没回来。
lose: Adrian只看了一眼就把手机扣回桌上，掌心沁出一层薄汗。心跳比偷看本身还响。
可那张十七岁的缩略图，已经印在他眼睛里了。
skip: Adrian把手机推回原位，指尖没碰屏幕。有些事，他想听Roman亲口说。

zh: 前舱门滑开，Roman回来了，带进一股冷气和淡淡的雪松须后水味。桌上的手机角度没变，屏幕亮度却不对。
他的灰眼睛在手机上停了半秒，又移到Adrian脸上。什么都没说，只是那半秒长得像一场审讯。

zh.hint: 他看过你的手机了。放得很仔细，角度一丝不差——仔细得像心虚。

opts.t: Roman和他对视了一秒，喉结滚了一下，什么都没问。
我的手机好看吗？
then: Adrian没眨眼，下巴微微一抬，胡茬底下压着一点笑。
Roman盯了他两秒，鼻腔里哼出一点气音，没再追问。

opts.t: Roman拿起手机，当着他的面改了密码。
then: 四个数字，他按得很慢，像故意让人看清。Adrian认得——便利店那晚的日期。

zh: Adrian正要开口，桌上那部手机又自己亮了。未知号码，语音消息，00:06。红点在屏幕角落一跳一跳。

zh.title: 语音消息 · 未知号码
zh.txt: 电流刮擦般失真的声音，冷得没有一点人味：“Cross，离他远点。”

zh: Roman整个人的气场变了。肩背绷直，眼神沉下去——不是害怕，是猎犬嗅到了血。
他拇指一划，语音被掐断。手背上青筋暴起，指节死死压在屏幕上，快得几乎带出风声。
快得更像是不想让Adrian听见。人藏东西只有两种原因：怕伤到自己，或者怕伤到你。
Cross。谁会这么叫他？我跟他一起长大，从没听过这个名字。

zh.hint: 他把语音掐了。你甚至没听清那个声音是男是女。

opts.t: 再放一遍。
它叫你Cross。它认识你。
then: Roman没回答。耳麦里传来细碎的电流声，他抬手按住，像按住一道伤口。

opts.t: Adrian伸手，宽厚的掌心整个覆住他握着手机的那只手。
then: Roman的手指僵了一下。掌心底下那只手背滚烫，青筋在Adrian手里突突地跳。他没抽走。

t: “离他远点。”七年前，也有人这么跟我说过。上一次，我听了——然后用七年来后悔。

zh: 飞机开始下降，耳膜一阵发胀。纽约从云层底下浮上来，灰蓝的楼群扎在正午的阳光里，像一片竖起的刀。
Roman起身扣好西装扣，把耳麦往耳道里又压了压。这一刻他不像谁的发小，像一堵会走路的墙。
舱门打开以后，站我左边。
因为外面有四十七张媒体证。
正午的泰特伯勒，停机坪被晒得发白，空气里全是航空煤油和热沥青的味道。
警戒线外挤着黑压压一片人，长焦镜头像一排架起的枪口，齐刷刷对准舷梯。
舱门开了。闪光灯先冲进来，白得发烫，喊声和快门声搅成一片。三小时前，他还是没人认识的上班族。
热风卷着尾气和人声灌进来。Adrian下意识眯起眼，那片白光扑上脸，像被人迎面泼了一盆滚水。
Roman向前半步，用整副肩背挡在他侧前方，一只大手落到他后腰。不是轻扶，是扣住。
隔着两层布料，那只手的热度直接烙进来。五指张开，掌根压住他的脊椎，稳得像一枚钉子。
四十七台镜头，他把手放在这儿。这人到底是来保护我的，还是来要我命的？

zh.hint: 四十七台镜头。你的手扣在他后腰，掌心底下是他绷紧的脊背——这个位置，不在任何安保手册里。

opts.t: （俯身到他耳边）走左边。贴紧我。
Roman把手从他后腰移到肩上，换成教科书式的护送姿势。
then: 隔着西装布料，Adrian反而觉得那只手太规矩了，规矩得让人心里发空。

opts.t: （贴着他耳后）别回头。你一回头，明天头条就是你的脸。
then: 扣在后腰的手收紧了一点，指节隔着衣料硌进他的腰窝。

zh: 温热的气息擦过耳后，Adrian的肩膀本能地绷紧，后颈的汗毛一根根竖了起来。
快门声暴雨一样砸下来。Adrian侧过脸，鼻尖几乎蹭上Roman的下颌，近到能闻见他领口的雪松味。
话筒一支支从人缝里戳过来，最近的那支几乎怼上他的下巴。
“时机烂透了。”Adrian咬着牙低声说。记者在喊：“你真的是秘密私生子吗？”“你已经订婚了吗？”

zh.title: 介入
zh.hint: 四十七台镜头，一个问题比一个狠。后腰那只手还扣着你——你要怎么站在这里？

then: Adrian只是笑了一下，下巴微扬，带着点布鲁克林式的混不吝。那张笑脸，第二天上了六家网站的首页。
扣在他后腰的手松了一点点，Roman的胸膛在他肩后轻轻一沉，像松了口气。
他对着最近的那支话筒说完，嗓音又低又稳，像钉进木头里的钉子，又补了一句——
全场死寂了一秒，然后快门声翻了一倍，像冰雹砸在铁皮屋顶上。
Roman低头看了他一眼，灰眼睛里沉着什么，深得看不见底。
谁告诉你们我今天落地的？
最前排的记者一愣，眼珠下意识往人群后面瞟了一眼。
Roman顺着那道视线看过去，眼神一冷，侧头对耳麦低声说了一句。

then.title: 线索：有人提前放了消息
then.txt: 落地时间，只有家族内部知道。

then: Adrian一把攥住Roman的手腕往身边一带，手背青筋绷起。Roman愣了半秒，顺势站到他身侧。
闪光灯像炸开一样，白光连成一片。这一张，明天会在所有人手机里。

zh.cap: 周三 12:41 · 舷梯上，他的手扣在你后腰
zh.prompt: Private jet stairs on a bright tarmac, dozens of camera flashes, a tall broad-shouldered man in a black suit with an earpiece shielding a broad-shouldered stubbled dark-haired man in a tailored suit, almost his height, his hand firmly at the other man's lower back, both in their late twenties, press crowd blurred in the foreground, cinematic, no text
then: Roman瞥了一眼照片，喉结动了一下，没让删。

zh: 车门“砰”地合上，把记者和热浪一起关在外面。冷气扑面，真皮座椅凉得发硬。
口袋里的手机开始失控地震，几十条，几百条，震得他大腿发麻。

zh.txt: Vale继承人现身，身边跟着神秘保镖。
cm: 这手放的位置也太离谱了。
他根本就是把人往自己怀里带。
没有保镖会这样看雇主。

zh: 放大后的照片比当时更暧昧。Roman的手指陷在他后腰的布料里，而照片里的自己往Roman那边偏着，一点都不像想躲。
互联网认识他们才十一分钟，就已经比他们两个都坦诚。
四万八千个赞。四万八千个陌生人，比我自己更早看出来我在往谁身上靠。
对面，Roman的动态刷新了：一张没有人的照片，酒店电梯的监控视角，灰白、冷硬。配文只有一句：镜头太多了。
Adrian抬眼。Roman正低头看平板，侧脸被车窗外的光切成明暗两半，耳麦线贴着脖颈，像什么都没发过。

zh.hint: 你可以在他的动态下面留言。半个纽约都在看——而他就坐在你对面，一臂之外。

opts.t: 你特别注意哪一个？
then: 评论发出去三秒，私聊就弹了出来。对面那人连头都没抬。
Adrian没删。他把手机往腿上一扣，冲Roman挑了挑眉。

opts.t: Adrian给那条动态点了个赞，什么都没写。
then: 小红心刚亮，私聊就来了。对面Roman的拇指还停在屏幕上。

opts.t: Adrian把那张媒体照存进了私人相册。
then: 没发，没赞，只是存了下来。他的拇指在照片里那只扣住他后腰的手上停了很久。
对面的Roman正在检查路线，眉心压出一道竖纹，完全不知道。

en: Forty-one thousand feet. The windows are packed with hard white glare; sunlight cuts across the cabin and lays a hot bar of gold over the walnut table.
The cream leather seats give off a sun-warmed smell, cut with the burnt bite of fresh coffee. The engines hum up through the soles of his boots; ice ticks against glass.
They both agree, without a word, that the last half second never happened. Roman sits. Adrian sits. Their chests are still going like they took five flights of stairs.
Roman leans back. Black suit cut close to the body, white shirt open at the throat by one button, a clear earpiece in his left ear, its coiled wire vanishing under the collar.
His dark hair is cropped almost to the scalp, his jaw rough with stubble. Grey eyes, cold as a frozen river. Right now they're very carefully not on Adrian.
Below the open collar, an old scar slants out from under his collarbone, paler than the skin around it. His black oxfords are polished enough to reflect the cabin lights.
Adrian is sunk in the seat opposite, all six feet of him filling the space between the armrests. The borrowed navy jacket strains across his shoulders; the seams bite every time he breathes.
His shirtsleeves are shoved to the elbow over thick forearms. On his feet, the same scuffed work boots with the toes rubbed bald, wildly out of place on this plane.
Great. Thirty seconds ago I nearly kissed my childhood best friend, and now I get to sit here admiring clouds. I write ad copy. I don't act.
He drags a hand over his unshaven jaw; the stubble rasps under his palm. His Adam's apple bobs as he forces the last ragged breath back down.
The inheritance tablet on the table wakes up on its own, throwing cold white light between them. One red line, dead center: SECONDARY IDENTITY VERIFICATION REQUIRED.
The first question slides up in a font so clean it's almost cruel: What does Adrian do when he's genuinely nervous?
Roman doesn't even lift his eyes. One finger taps once against his knee.
Adrian looks down. His right hand is already wrapped around his left wrist, a rough thumb working the knob of bone, slow and steady.
A habit he never noticed himself. Ten whole years, and Roman still knows it like he saw it yesterday.
Hell. He remembers that. So what else is he still carrying around?

en.hint: The check needs both of you. The tablet swivels, and its cold light lands on your face. Your turn to answer about him.

qs.q: What fruit does Roman hate most?
After a fight, who apologizes first?
How does Roman take his coffee?

win.title: MATCH 92%
win.txt: Ninety-two. Nobody memorizes another man down to the bone by accident.

win: The tablet bursts into a ring of pink light. It flares in Roman's grey eyes and dies.
The missing eight is the years I wasn't there.
lose: The bar stalls on an in-between number and blinks twice. Roman glances at it. His Adam's apple moves. He says nothing.
But every question he answered, he got right. He even knew which bone Adrian rubs when he's rattled.
skip: Skip it. I know the answers.

en.hint: The check ends, and a pink door slides in from the edge of the screen: Couple Q&A. Three private questions. Answer or skip. It looks exactly like a trap.

opts.t: What did you miss most?
then: Roman takes a long time. He looks out at all that white, jaw set in a hard clean line, before he finally speaks.
You yelling at me. Nobody else ever dared.

opts.t: Who looked away first that night?
then: Roman's jaw locks. A muscle rolls under the stubble. He doesn't argue.

opts.t: Adrian jabs Skip with his thumb.
then: Roman watches the Skip button go grey. His shoulders drop half an inch, and something behind his eyes dims right along with it.

en: Another animation, all gold foil, floods up from the bottom of the screen: WELCOME BENEFIT / PERSONAL GIFT CREDIT.
The first item is a $40,000 watch, its platinum case glaring in the render. Yesterday he'd never have opened the page. Today it's suggested like a cup of coffee.
But a price tag has never impressed Roman. He just wants to see Roman happy. The thought arrives so smoothly it's deeply inconvenient.
Get a grip, Adrian. He's on the clock. You're the job.

en.title: Gift Guess
en.hint: The most expensive isn't always right. Your finger hovers over the glass. How much of him do you still remember?

then: Roman shoves his cuff back. A tanned wrist, and across the inside of it, an old scar gone pale.
Adrian buckles the strap for him. His fingertip drags across the scar. Hot skin, and under it a pulse knocking against his finger.
You know I can do that myself.
Adrian presses the clasp home. Click. Only then does he look up.
I wanted to see if it looked good on you.
Roman looks at the faded cloth cover. His fingers stop on the cracked spine, knuckles going white.
He opens it. His name is still on the flyleaf in a seventeen-year-old's ballpoint, pressed so hard it tore the paper. He shuts it and is quiet a long time.
items.sub: The one he wore out at seventeen

then: You know I touch my wrist when I'm nervous. We're even.
Roman slides the card into his inside pocket, the side over his heart, and flattens it there with his palm.
Roman lifts the cufflinks to the light; the engraving throws back a cold glint. He studies them a long time, but his eyes keep sliding to the Vale crest cufflink on the table.
Same maker. Where did you order these?
His jaw tightens. A vein rises at his temple.
I can't wear these on the job.
Then wear them off the job.
Roman holds the earbuds and blinks, like it has never once occurred to him that he has an 'off the job.'
items.sub: For a man who's always listening

en: Roman digs an old keychain out of his jacket and sets it in Adrian's palm. The brass is rubbed bright, the edges worn round, still warm from his body.
Adrian closes his fist around it. The metal digs into the calluses on his palm, and that leftover warmth climbs straight up his forearm.

en.title: Memory: The Keychain He Never Threw Away
en.txt: Obviously a lie. Brass doesn't wear like that unless you've been holding it for years.

en: Adrian is about to ask how long, when the phone in his pocket jolts. A gold banner swallows the screen: FIANCÉ ARRIVAL — 18:00.
There's a photo attached. Honey-blond hair combed into perfect order, a charcoal three-piece suit, the waistcoat buttoned all the way up.
A signet ring gleams on the hand folded over his knee. He smiles for the camera exactly as much as required, like something in a luxury window. Even the smile has a price tag.
A fiancée. I haven't even figured out my own bank account yet, and apparently I've got a fiancée.
His eyes travel from FIANCÉ to Roman's face. Nothing moves there. Only the hand on the table's edge has stopped, knuckles pulled white.

en.hint: A fiancée out of thin air. More interesting than the fiancée: Roman's frozen hand.

opts.t: Hot?

then.hint: "Hot?" He's doing it on purpose. You know he's watching how you answer.

opts.t: Irrelevant.
Not as good as me.
then: Adrian stares for a beat, then laughs, a low rough sound straight from the chest.
I said he lands at six.

opts.t: Roman switches his phone screen off. "I'll find out who he is."
then: Checking him out, or guarding against him?

opts.t: If I get married, are you running security for that too?
then: Two seconds of silence. Nothing in the cabin but the low drone of the engines.
I'll make sure he leaves your building alive.

opts.t: Adrian doesn't ask anything. He just watches Roman's frozen hand.
then: Roman draws the hand back and closes it slowly into a fist. The veins on the back of it stand up one by one.
Look at that hand. His mouth won't give me a thing, but those veins are confessing everything.

en: The captain's voice comes from up front: landing security needs his sign-off. Roman stands, jacket falling sharp into place, takes two steps, and turns back.
You say that like I'm six.
On the corner of the table, Roman's black encrypted phone lights up. A thumbnail flashes past: Adrian at seventeen, grinning like nothing could ever touch him.
He shouldn't look. The other half of his brain says: he watched you behind your back for three years. 'Fair' is suddenly a very handy word.
Adrian's hand moves before his brain signs off. His big palm comes down over the phone, fingertips still holding the keychain's warmth.

en.hint: He's up front; his low voice leaks through the door. The screen's unlocked. You have maybe a minute.

items: He still doesn't know, does he?
How long are you going to keep this up?
If he comes home, you failed.

apps.lockTxt: Passcode required. Hint: the date of the convenience-store night.
items: Adrian and Roman at seventeen and eighteen, on the curb outside the store. Adrian hasn't learned the sharp smile yet. Roman hasn't learned to hide anything.
Saved ten years ago. Opened once a year since, on the same date.
I should have told him before today.
Unsent · 3 years ago / 1 year ago / yesterday
Wed 08:05 · Pick up A. Go yourself.
Directions · a convenience store in Brooklyn · 41 times

win: He sets the phone back exactly where it was, same angle, even the window glare lined up on the glass.
He kept that photo. For ten years.
The draft is worse than the photo. It means he thought about coming back. He just didn't, again and again.
lose: Adrian looks once and turns the phone face down, palms gone damp. His heartbeat is louder than the snooping.
But the thumbnail of his seventeen-year-old face is already burned in.
skip: Adrian pushes the phone back without touching the glass. Some things he wants to hear out of Roman's own mouth.

en: The cabin door slides open and Roman comes back with a draft of cold air and a trace of cedar aftershave. The phone's at the same angle. The brightness isn't.
His grey eyes rest on the phone for half a second, then move to Adrian's face. He says nothing. That half second lasts as long as an interrogation.

en.hint: He's been through your phone. He put it back carefully, angle perfect. Carefully enough to look guilty.

opts.t: Roman holds his eyes for a second, swallows, and asks nothing.
Enjoy my phone?
then: Adrian doesn't blink. His chin lifts a fraction, a grin held down under the stubble.
Roman stares at him for two seconds, lets out a short breath through his nose, and drops it.

opts.t: Roman picks up the phone and changes the passcode right in front of him.
then: Four digits, punched in slow, like he wants them seen. Adrian knows them. The date of the convenience-store night.

en: Adrian opens his mouth, and the phone lights up again on its own. Unknown number. Voice message, 00:06. A red dot pulses in the corner.

en.title: Voice Message · Unknown Number
en.txt: A voice scraped raw by distortion, nothing human left in it: "Cross, walk away."

en: Something in Roman switches over. Spine straight, eyes gone flat. Not fear. A hound catching blood on the wind.
One swipe of his thumb and the message is dead. The veins stand out across the back of his hand, knuckles pinning the screen, so fast it almost cuts the air.
Fast enough that it's about Adrian not hearing. People hide things for two reasons: it could hurt them, or it could hurt you.
Cross. Who calls him that? I grew up with the man, and I've never once heard that name.

en.hint: He killed it. You didn't even catch whether the voice was a man's or a woman's.

opts.t: Play it again.
It called you Cross. It knows you.
then: A lot of people know me.
A lot of people tell you to stay away from me?
Roman doesn't answer. Static crackles in his earpiece; he presses two fingers to it like he's holding a wound shut.

opts.t: Adrian reaches over and covers the hand holding the phone with his whole broad palm.
then: Roman's fingers lock. The back of his hand is burning under Adrian's palm, a vein jumping against it. He doesn't pull away.
I didn't ask if you were fine.

t: 'Walk away.' Someone told me that seven years ago. Last time, I listened. I've spent seven years paying for it.

en: They start down; his ears pop and ache. New York rises out from under the clouds, grey-blue towers standing in the noon sun like a rack of upturned blades.
Roman stands, buttons his jacket, and presses the earpiece deeper. In that moment he isn't anybody's childhood friend. He's a wall that walks.
When the door opens, stay on my left.
Because there are forty-seven press credentials outside.
Teterboro at noon. The tarmac is baked white, the air thick with jet fuel and hot asphalt.
Beyond the barrier, a black mass of bodies. Long lenses line up like a row of rifle barrels, every one trained on the stairs.
The door opens. The flashes hit first, white and scalding, then the shouting and the shutters, all one roar. Three hours ago, nobody knew his name.
Hot wind barrels in, full of exhaust and voices. Adrian squints on reflex; the white light hits his face like a pot of boiling water thrown point-blank.
Roman steps half a pace ahead and to the side, putting the whole wall of his shoulders in the way, and one big hand lands at the small of Adrian's back. Not resting. Holding.
Through two layers of cloth the heat of that hand brands straight in. Fingers spread, the heel of the palm pinned to his spine, steady as a driven nail.
Forty-seven cameras, and that's where he puts his hand. Is he here to protect me or to finish me off?

en.hint: Forty-seven cameras. Your hand is locked at the small of his back, his spine rigid under your palm. No security manual puts it there.

opts.t: (at his ear) Left side. Stay close.
Roman moves his hand from Adrian's back to his shoulder. Textbook escort position.
then: Through the wool, Adrian finds the hand almost too correct. Correct enough to leave a hollow behind.

opts.t: (right at his ear) Don't turn around. Turn around and your face is tomorrow's front page.
then: The hand at his back tightens, knuckles pressing through the fabric into the dip of his spine.

en: Warm breath grazes the back of his ear. Adrian's shoulders lock on instinct; the hair on his nape stands up.
The shutters come down like a cloudburst. Adrian turns his head and his nose nearly brushes Roman's jaw, close enough to smell cedar at his collar.
Microphones jab through the gaps in the crowd, one after another; the nearest one nearly clips his chin.
"Terrible timing," Adrian says through his teeth. The press is shouting: "ARE YOU THE SECRET SON?" "ARE YOU ENGAGED?"

en.title: Step In as Adrian
en.hint: Forty-seven cameras, each question nastier than the last. That hand is still locked at your back. How do you stand here?

then: Adrian just smiles, chin up, pure Brooklyn don't-care. By tomorrow, that smile is on six front pages.
The hand at his back eases a fraction. Behind his shoulder, Roman's chest settles, like a breath let go.
He says it into the nearest mic, voice low and level as a nail going into wood, then adds —
One second of dead silence. Then the shutters double, hail on a tin roof.
Roman looks down at him, and something sits in those grey eyes, too deep to see the bottom of.
Who told you I was landing today?
The front-row reporter freezes, and his eyes flick, without permission, toward the back of the crowd.
Roman follows the look. His eyes go cold, and he turns his head to say something low into the earpiece.

then.title: Clue: Someone Tipped Them Off
then.txt: Only the family knew when he'd land.

then: Adrian grabs Roman's wrist and hauls him level, tendons standing up across the back of his hand. Roman freezes half a second, then steps in at his side.
The flashes go off like a detonation, one solid sheet of white. This one will be on every phone by morning.
(very low) You did that on purpose.

en.cap: Wed 12:41 · On the stairs, his hand at your back
en.prompt: Private jet stairs on a bright tarmac, dozens of camera flashes, a tall broad-shouldered man in a black suit with an earpiece shielding a broad-shouldered stubbled dark-haired man in a tailored suit, almost his height, his hand firmly at the other man's lower back, both in their late twenties, press crowd blurred in the foreground, cinematic, no text
then: Roman glances at the photo. His throat works. He doesn't tell you to delete it.

en: The car door slams, shutting out the press and the heat together. Cold air hits his face; the leather seat is chilled stiff.
The phone in his pocket goes haywire. Dozens of notifications. Hundreds. His thigh goes numb from the buzzing.

en.txt: Vale heir spotted with mystery bodyguard.
cm: He is literally pulling him into his body.
That is not how a bodyguard looks at a client.

en: Blown up, the photo is worse than the moment. Roman's fingers are sunk into the fabric at his back, and in it Adrian is leaning toward him. He doesn't look like he wants to get away.
The internet has known them for eleven minutes and is already less subtle than either of them.
Forty-eight thousand likes. Forty-eight thousand strangers spotted who I was leaning into before I did.
Across from him, Roman's feed refreshes: a photo with no people in it, a hotel elevator from the security camera's angle, grey and hard. Caption: Too many cameras.
Adrian looks up. Roman is bent over his tablet, profile split into light and shadow by the window, earpiece wire against his neck, like he never posted a thing.

en.hint: You can comment under his post. Half of New York is watching. And he's sitting an arm's length across from you.

opts.t: You noticed one in particular?
then: Three seconds after it posts, a DM pops up. The man across from him hasn't even lifted his head.
Adrian doesn't. He drops the phone face down on his thigh and raises an eyebrow at Roman.

opts.t: Adrian likes the post and writes nothing.
then: The heart has barely turned red when the DM lands. Across the car, Roman's thumb is still on his screen.

opts.t: Adrian saves the press photo to a private album.
then: No post, no like. He just keeps it, his thumb resting a long time on the hand locked at his back.
Across from him, Roman is checking the route, one hard crease between his brows, with no idea.
